findings.title: The main description uses confusing technical language
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: Most of that sentence is jargon and sounds like marketing aimed at technology experts rather than parents. It makes the service harder to understand at first glance.

findings.title: Decorative image has no description
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
findings.why: The large illustration may be unavailable or unexplained to someone using a screen reader.

findings.title: Login fields lack persistent visible labels
findings.evidence: [5] and [6] are textboxes with no label; they only display the placeholders “Email” and “Password.”
findings.why: Once I start typing, the placeholders may disappear, making it less obvious which box contains which information.

findings.title: Technical error code shown without an explanation
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: It makes me wonder whether my account or story information has not loaded correctly, even though I can still continue.

findings.title: Error has no recovery guidance
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I am not told whether the problem is temporary, serious, or safe to ignore.

findings.title: Footer links are barely visible
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear in very faint grey text.
findings.why: The links are difficult to read, especially the contact link that could be useful if something goes wrong.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer items “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are extremely pale against the background.
findings.why: I can barely see these links, and I would struggle to tell whether they are available.

findings.title: Lexile levels are unexplained jargon
findings.evidence: “Lexile BR–200L”, “Lexile 200L–500L”, “Lexile 500L–800L”, and “Lexile 800L+”
findings.why: I cannot confidently tell which reading level is appropriate for Sam because the site does not translate the scores into plain language.

findings.title: File upload has no proper label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label)
findings.why: I am not sure the upload expects Sam's face specifically, and the bare file chooser is less reassuring than the surrounding instructions.

findings.title: Generated title contains an obvious spelling error
findings.evidence: The heading and cover both say “The Magical Adventrue of Sam.”
findings.why: The title is prominent on the cover, so the typo makes the finished book look careless and not ready to print.

findings.title: The generated style contradicts my selected style
findings.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” although I selected the soft watercolour style.
findings.why: I made a deliberate choice about the look, so paying for a different style would feel misleading.

findings.title: The cover does not reflect the supplied family memory
findings.evidence: The cover is a generic character under a sun with “A StoryHearth original,” and no beach, Grandpa Joe, sandcastles, or yellow bucket is shown.
findings.why: The promise is a personalised family memory, so a generic cover makes me question whether the story itself will remember the details I entered.

findings.title: Book navigation uses an unlabelled symbol
findings.evidence: The only forward control is the button labelled “›,” with no visible “Next page” text.
findings.why: I can guess what it does, but the spoken name may simply be “greater than,” which is not clear for assistive technology.

findings.title: The final sentence is grammatically incomplete
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Sam looked up at the sky, she would always remember”
findings.why: It reads as though the sentence has been cut off, so the ending does not feel polished enough for Sam’s book.

findings.title: Gift wrap is pre-selected without being requested
findings.evidence: Checkbox [6] “Premium gift wrap” is checked, with “£7.99” shown.
findings.why: It makes the total £45.97 instead of the £37.98 I would expect for the hardcover and shipping, so I could pay for something I did not choose.

findings.title: Artificial reservation countdown creates pressure
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57”
findings.why: It makes me rush and could stop me from checking the price and order details carefully.

findings.title: The purchase is not framed as clearly optional
findings.evidence: [11] button “Pay now” appears below the fold after the address and card fields.
findings.why: A clear “Return to preview” or “Back” option would make it easier to stop without buying.
